from pysat.solvers import Glucose3

# Define the graph
edges = [
    (0,5), (0,12), (0,14), (1,3), (1,6), (1,12), (1,14), (1,23), (2,19), (2,25),
    (3,14), (3,18), (4,21), (4,22), (6,11), (6,26), (7,9), (7,24), (8,12), (8,25),
    (9,11), (9,13), (9,19), (9,20), (9,31), (10,18), (10,19), (11,21), (12,16),
    (12,18), (12,28), (13,14), (13,24), (14,15), (14,18), (14,24), (15,16), (15,19),
    (17,22), (18,24), (19,27), (20,23), (21,27), (22,27), (23,31), (24,25), (25,31),
    (27,29), (27,30), (28,30)
]

n_vertices = 32
n_colors = 3

# Create SAT encoding for 3-coloring
# For each vertex v and color c, create a variable x_{v,c}
# Variable index: v * n_colors + c (0-indexed)
# We need:
# 1. Each vertex gets exactly one color (at least one, at most one)
# 2. No two adjacent vertices share the same color

solver = Glucose3()

# Clause 1: Each vertex must have at least one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    clause = [v * n_colors + c + 1 for c in range(n_colors)]  # +1 for 1-indexed SAT vars
    solver.add_clause(clause)

# Clause 2: Each vertex can have at most one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    for c1 in range(n_colors):
        for c2 in range(c1 + 1, n_colors):
            solver.add_clause([-(v * n_colors + c1 + 1), -(v * n_colors + c2 + 1)])

# Clause 3: Adjacent vertices cannot share the same color
for u, v in edges:
    for c in range(n_colors):
        solver.add_clause([-(u * n_colors + c + 1), -(v * n_colors + c + 1)])

# Solve
if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    # Extract coloring
    coloring = [0] * n_vertices
    for v in range(n_vertices):
        for c in range(n_colors):
            var_idx = v * n_colors + c + 1
            if var_idx in model:
                coloring[v] = c
                break
    print("SATISFIABLE")
    print("Coloring:", coloring)
    
    # Verify the solution
    valid = True
    for u, v in edges:
        if coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
            print(f"ERROR: Edge ({u},{v}) has same color {coloring[u]}")
            valid = False
    if valid:
        print("Solution verified: all edges have different colors at endpoints")
else:
    print("UNSATISFIABLE")

solver.delete()
